input.reasoning_summary: All three challenges are refuted by the evidence. H1 sought to distinguish boilerplate language from actual material risks, but E7 explicitly discusses "outstanding legal matters" (not hypothetical future ones) and states they could have a material adverse effect. H2 sought evidence that no legal matters pose material risk, but E7 directly contradicts this by stating outstanding matters could have material adverse effect. While E5 notes Russia-related matters specifically are not expected to have material adverse effect, this is only one subset of legal matters. H3 sought to show the language is conditional and refers to hypothetical future claims, but E7 clearly refers to "outstanding matters" and "Certain outstanding matters" that currently exist and seek substantial monetary amounts or remedies. The evidence review confirms E7 CONTRADICTS the claim with EXACT_MATCH period compatibility and HISTORICAL_FACT statement time. The claim asserts legal and regulatory matters "do not pose a material risk" but the September 30, 2026 10-Q explicitly states outstanding legal matters "could, either individually or in aggregate, have a material adverse effect." This is a direct contradiction of the claim's assertion.
